records.label: Patient with de novo FBRSL1 p.Ala128Cysfs*5
quotes: We identified a de novo FBRSL1 variant p.Ala128Cysfs*5 in a patient with neurodevelopmental delay, epilepsy, congenital heart disease, and facial dysmorphism.

notes.statement: Xu et al. (2026) analyzed 4 patients with FBRSL1 variants and described an emerging syndromic neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by microcephaly, global developmental delay, autism, facial dysmorphism, and skeletal contractures.
quotes: Further analysis of four patients with FBRSL1 variants revealed an emerging syndromic NDD, characterized by microcephaly, global developmental delay, autism, facial dysmorphism, and skeletal contractures.

notes.statement: Xu et al. (2026) found that fbrsl1 knockdown in zebrafish recapitulated neurodevelopmental abnormalities, epileptiform discharges, and cardiac dysfunction, consistent with the phenotype of a patient carrying a de novo FBRSL1 truncating variant.
quotes: Zebrafish knockdown models recapitulated neurodevelopmental abnormalities, epileptiform discharges, and cardiac dysfunction, consistent with the patient's phenotypes.

notes.statement: Xu et al. (2026) found that FBRSL1 is highly expressed in the developing brain and heart, which could potentially explain the multisystem phenotypes. Single-cell RNA sequencing showed high FBRSL1 expression in neural progenitors of 1-month-old brain organoids.
quotes: FBRSL1 is highly expressed in the developing brain and heart, potentially explaining its multisystem phenotypes.
Single-cell RNA sequencing revealed a high expression of FBRSL1 in neural progenitors of 1-month-old organoids, suggesting its vital role in neurodevelopment.

notes.statement: Bukvic et al. (2024) found that SNP array in their patient with a de novo FBRSL1 frameshift variant also showed a paternal duplication of about 530 kb at 7p11.2 and 2 maternal duplications at 16p13.11. All 3 were classified as variants of uncertain significance. STITCH in silico analysis found no interactions that could explain the phenotype.
quotes: All three microduplications (2 mat and 1 pat, respectively) were considered as variants of uncertain significance (VUS).
However, neither of these could be consequently traced back to the clinical phenotype or to a particular symptomatology of our patient.

notes.statement: Bukvic et al. (2024) predicted that the truncated 131-residue FBRSL1 protein keeps a self-binding domain (residues 81 to 93) and nuclear localization signals. From this they hypothesized that it could bind and inactivate wildtype FBRSL1, acting as a dominant negative.
quotes: The truncated version found in the patient, which shows two nuclear localization signals, could localize in the nucleus, and thanks to the self-binding domain formed by amino acid residues 81–93, interact with the wild-type isoforms of FBRSL1, inactivating them. This could confer a possible negative dominance effect on the mutation in our case.

notes.statement: Bukvic et al. (2024) found that the genome-wide DNA methylation profile (EpiSign) in peripheral blood of a patient with a truncating FBRSL1 variant matched controls for all episignatures tested, including the PRC2 episignature. FBRSL1 and PRC1.5 episignatures have not yet been defined.
quotes: EpiSign assessment of the patient revealed a genome-wide DNA methylation profile that aligned with negative controls across all episignatures evaluated, including the one associated with the polycomb repressive complex 2 (PRC2), as indicated by an MVP score of zero.

notes.statement: Bukvic et al. (2024) noted features in their patient that had not been reported in the 3 earlier FBRSL1 cases: epilepsy, stereotypies, hip dislocation, chewing problems, and need for percutaneous endoscopic gastrostomy. Seizures responded at first to valproic acid but later relapsed, and ethosuximide and rufinamide were added.
quotes: Valproic acid (VPA) was administered early with immediately good control of seizures, but months later, the patient underwent a relapse with daily drop tonic seizures and myoclonic absences, so ethosuximide and rufinamide were added to valproic acid with better but not complete control.

notes.statement: Pauli et al. (2021) reviewed the 3 previously reported patients with truncating FBRSL1 variants. In the neonatal period they had respiratory insufficiency and feeding difficulties. Later they developed intellectual disability with no active speech, postnatal microcephaly, growth retardation and contractures. Two had cleft palate and heart defects, one had asplenia, one had anal atresia, and the 2 more severely affected patients had congenital skin creases that disappeared during the first year of life.
quotes: The patients presented with respiratory insufficiency and feeding difficulties in the neonatal period. During infancy, intellectual disability, no active speech, postnatal microcephaly, growth retardation and contractures became apparent.

In one patient asplenia and in another patient anal atresia were observed. Furthermore, the two more severely affected patients were born with pronounced congenital skin creases at the back, the arms, and legs.

notes.statement: Pauli et al. (2021) used the AUTS2 syndrome severity scoring system to compare the FBRSL1 patients with patients with AUTS2 syndrome. They found a remarkable overlap with the severe form of AUTS2 syndrome, but the FBRSL1 patients had a wider spectrum and higher rate of congenital malformations.
quotes: A remarkable overlap between the two syndromes was observed with a wider spectrum and higher rate of congenital malformations in children with a pathogenic variant in FBRSL1.
we also used the ASSS to compare the phenotype of the three patients with a variant in FBRSL1 (Ufartes et al., 2020) to patients with AUTS2 syndrome (Table 1).

notes.statement: Pauli et al. (2021) noted that severe AUTS2 syndrome is linked to C-terminal AUTS2 variants. In contrast, all 3 FBRSL1 patients had truncating variants in the N-terminus of FBRSL1 (2 stop variants and 1 frameshift) that affect the short N-terminal isoforms.
quotes: all three patients harbor a truncating variant (stop mutation in two patients and a frameshift variant with premature stop codon in the other patient) in the N-terminus of FBRSL1 affecting the short N-terminal isoforms (Ufartes et al., 2020).

notes.statement: Pauli et al. (2021) reviewed data showing that morpholino knockdown of Fbrsl1 in Xenopus caused craniofacial defects, cartilage hypoplasia, reduced brain size, and impaired migration of cranial nerves and motor neurons. A human short N-terminal FBRSL1 isoform rescued the craniofacial defects. Neither a patient-variant version of that isoform nor the long isoform rescued them, suggesting that mutations of the short N-terminal isoforms are causative.
quotes: Morpholino-mediated Fbrsl1 knockdown resulted in craniofacial defects and the embryos showed cartilage hypoplasia as well as a reduction in brain size on the injected side (Figures 1A–C).
However, neither a patient variant of this isoform nor the long FBRSL1 isoform, which both lack the Ftsk domain, were able to rescue the morphant phenotype (Ufartes et al., 2020).

notes.statement: Pauli et al. (2021) noted that, like AUTS2, FBRSL1 interacts with Polycomb subcomplexes PRC1.3 and PRC1.5 and competes with AUTS2 for binding to PRC1.5. FBRSL1 was found in both the nucleus and the cytoplasm of HEK293 cells and human fibroblasts. An N-terminal antibody detected both nuclear and cytoplasmic FBRSL1, whereas a C-terminal antibody detected mainly nuclear FBRSL1.
quotes: Like AUTS2, FBRSL1 was also identified by tandem affinity purification and mass spectrometry as an interaction partner of PRC1.3 and PRC1.5 (Gao et al., 2012). Further, it was shown that FBRSL1 competes with AUTS2 for binding to the PRC1.5 complex (Gao et al., 2014).

mainly a nuclear FBRSL1 pattern was detected with an antibody directed against the C-terminal part of FBRSL1, while nuclear and cytoplasmic FBRSL1 was observed with an antibody targeted against the N-terminal part of the protein

notes.statement: Pauli et al. (2021) described a long 19-exon FBRSL1 transcript (NM_001142641.2) and 2 validated short N-terminal isoforms. The short isoforms contain an alternative exon 3 that leads to a stop codon; they lack the AUTS2 family domain but include a predicted Ftsk DNA translocase domain.
quotes: The two short isoforms contain an alternative exon three leading to a stop codon. These two short N-terminal forms lack the homologous AUTS2 family domain, but include a predicted DNA translocase domain (Ftsk)
